annotations.text:
New structure, borrowed from how Labour Link separates its products.

Landing (left): hero unchanged; the three door cards are gone. Nav = Ghar · Kaam · Sabha · How it works · Login. Under the hero a compact strip names the three portals; further down each gets its own audience section (For households / For workers / For the council) with four points and an Explore button — this replaces the old “Four things” cards. Footer gains a Portals column.

Login (right): the common gateway at /app/login. Pick who you are → that portal’s own sign-in. Accounts are per portal; a Ghar login can never open Kaam or Sabha.

One portal, end to end: public landing (/app/ghar) → sign-in → sign-up (name, mobile, locality, password) → the existing Ghar screen, now signed in.

Inside the portal there is no “All portals” link any more — only the user’s initials and Sign out, which returns to /app/ghar. Kaam and Sabha follow the same four-page shape in their own colour.

Kaam sign-up is Hindi-first like the rest of Kaam, and collects what the allocation engine needs: trades, area, languages. Creating the account creates the worker record.

Sabha sign-up is desktop-shaped and gated: the council code is the first field and is checked before anything else. Anyone without it cannot create a council account. [Council code shown is a sample.]
